"Disgusting creatures,." Yuna glossed over the countless Flora, busy working away making patterns. "And to think that they were created to be the peaceful species of this planet. Yet they've become a bringer of chaos to this world, creating countless patterns and designs. Those designs by themselves are fine, but they've become obsessed."

The light crept through a hole leading into a Flora workshop. "Obsessed with designing patterns and gaining knowledge. Forcing themselves to work days on end without rest, all to fix one small problem. They were never meant to do this. This is not what they were created for."

Off of countless plates of rounded metal, light reflected, filling the room. "They learned many things. They were the makers of the first machines, upon which they used to improve their lives. Then the idea of currency was bestowed unto them."

A ring of bloomed flowers is heated by the light. "Greed. They learned their first deadly sin. But there was no way for them to stop. They were controlled by their greed, it was an instinct for them. I thought I could protect them, that they would, would live lives in peace, without ever living through war."

Inside the Tree of Life the light grew blinding. "But no, I couldn't. I was too stupid. They were created with free will, to not be a hivemind. They could choose their own god, they weren't born worshiping me. They built their own path. This path led to the tragedies currently unfolding."

"Why did I create such a free being? Why would other gods wish ill motives on them? Why have they become the opposite of what they were meant to be? I, I need to think about this. There must be a way to fix it, to stop the damage the Flora have caused from worsening."

An old branch fell from inside the Tree of Life and hit the ground, snapping in two."Well then... that's one option. It would solve the problems the Flora have created, and prevent more from arising..."

----------

Around the Tree of Life, home of the Flora, where the land is pure and peaceful, the sky grew dark. Yuna's light, normally keeping the place lit day and night, was not gone. No, it was still there, it had never left in fact. Yuna's light had grown dark, and the effects of it were immediate.

Flora in and around the Tree of Life collapsed, souls leaving them for the Realm of Death. There was no more Flora at the Tree of Life, sans the few masters of their skill and craft, having watched their friends and family perish before them.

A hazy purple light shone in the dark sky. Yuna's voice boomed, "Those of you that remain, listen to my words. You are to teach what you have learned to the next creatures I create. Your species has become corrupt and disastrous, your actions brought this upon yourselves. This will serve as a warning to creatures to come, that if they become too disastrous for this world, that I will personally remove them."

And with that, the light faded away, the sky turning back to what it was before. Yet something was missing, be it Yuna's light, or the Flora civilization that had lived there moments before.
